notification.summary: The AISSEE 2026 cycle is complete: the exam was held on 18 Jan 2026 in pen-and-paper mode and results were declared on 27 Feb 2026. The information bulletin for AISSEE 2027 (admission 2027-28) had not been released as of 10 Oct 2026. Based on past cycles (AISSEE 2026 registration opened on 10 Oct 2025), registration is expected in Oct–Nov 2026 and the exam in Jan 2027.

pattern.notes: Mathematics questions carry 3 marks each; Language, Intelligence and GK questions carry 2 marks each (pattern.marking shows the 2-mark default). There is no negative marking. The paper is available in English, Hindi and 11 other regional languages; this mock uses English for the Language section. Candidates need at least 25% in each subject and 40% overall (not applicable to SC/ST). Intelligence questions that use figures in the real paper are given here as text equivalents.

trendAnalysis.summary: Based on the Jan-2024, Apr-2025 and Jan-2026 Class 6 papers. Mathematics carries half the marks and decides the merit. It sticks to the official topic list (unitary method, LCM/HCF, fractions, profit-loss, SI, speed-time, area-perimeter, angles, Roman numerals, temperature and unit conversion) at moderate difficulty, with more multi-step word problems in recent years. Intelligence is easy: series, analogy, coding, classification and a few figure-based items. GK mixes basic science, Indian history and geography, defence-related facts and recent events. Language tests basic grammar, vocabulary and a short comprehension. Time pressure is real (125 questions in 150 minutes), so speed in Maths is key.

pyqBlueprint.method: Compiled from the Class VI papers of AISSEE 2024 (Jan 2024), 2025 (Apr 2025) and 2026 (18 Jan 2026) as reproduced in NTA provisional answer-key booklets, Careers360 question-paper pages and coaching solved-paper compilations (found via web search, Oct 2026), together with the official Class VI syllabus topic list and the writer's own knowledge of these papers. Official booklets could not be fetched in this session, so patterns are summarised from these sources and memory; frequencies are approximate per paper.

archetypes.pattern: Short story/factual passage; direct-detail question (number, name, place) answered from one sentence
Inference/reason question on the same passage (why, what lesson, how someone felt)
Word closest in meaning (synonym) to a common adjective/verb
Word opposite in meaning (antonym); distractors include synonyms
Meaning of a word or gender/feminine form of a noun
Fill in the blank with the correct preposition/article
Fill in the blank with the correct tense/verb form (time marker in the sentence)
Nouns and parts of speech: plurals, collective nouns, identify adjective/adverb in a sentence
Choose the correctly spelt word among four variants
One word for a phrase (person/place)
Rearrange jumbled words into a correct sentence
Primes, factors and number facts (count/sum of primes in a range, smallest prime)
Convert or add Roman numerals (subtractive forms XL, XC, CM)
LCM word problem: bells ringing together, least number arranged in rows
HCF word problem: greatest length/size that measures or divides exactly
Compare or add/subtract fractions and mixed numbers
Decimal addition/subtraction/multiplication with place-value traps
Unitary method: cost of n items; workers–days (inverse proportion)
Divide a sum or total in a given ratio
x% of y, find the whole from a part, marks percentage, simple growth
SP/CP from profit or loss %, total profit on quantities
SI = PRT/100 with fractional years
Average of a list or of consecutive numbers
Distance/time in minutes; speed in km/h ↔ m/s
Perimeter/area of rectangle and square, cost of fencing, tiles needed
Volume of cube/cuboid; number of small cubes in a box
Complementary/supplementary angles and angle sum of a triangle
Angle between clock hands at whole hours; types of angles
Circumference/area/diameter of a circle with π = 22/7
Celsius ↔ Fahrenheit conversion
Metric unit conversion (L–mL, km–m, kg–g)
Pie chart: sector angle ↔ percentage/amount; read values from a bar graph
Word analogy (tool–function, worker–tool)
Number analogy (square, cube, n² + 1)
Odd one out among words or numbers (category, prime/square)
Number series (squares + 1, ×n, factorial-type growth)
Letter series with fixed skips or letter pairs
Letter-shift coding (+1/−1) applied to a new word
Reversal or number-value coding (sum of letter positions)
Turns and walks; final direction or straight-line distance
Two- or three-step family relation
Mirror image of letters/digits/words; which stays the same
Total in a row/class from positions at both ends
Who built a monument / which ruler is linked to an event
Freedom fighters: titles, slogans and roles
State capitals, continents and oceans
Solar system and space facts
Human body and plants; basic science facts
National symbols, wildlife and environment
Constitution, important posts and national days
Players per team, trophies and the sport they belong to
Gallantry awards and defence training institutions
Ranks, warships and indigenous defence equipment
Author of a famous book/song
A major national achievement of the previous year (space, sports, defence)

resources.notes: NTA publishes the provisional answer key together with the question paper and the candidate's recorded responses for challenge on exams.nta.nic.in/sainik-school-society after each exam, and later the final key. The information bulletin includes the syllabus and topic-wise marks list. Past papers are also compiled by publishers.
